Infill Missing Depth Variability

Source: R/depth-simulation.R
infill_missing_depth_variability.Rd

Infills missing depth variability values in a horizon data frame by replacing missing top and bottom depth bounds with the representative depth value plus or minus 2, ensuring that the resulting values are not negative.

Usage

infill_missing_depth_variability(horizon_data)

Arguments

horizon_data

A data frame containing horizon depth data. It must include the following columns:

  • hzdept_r: Representative top depth.

  • hzdept_l: Top low value (may be missing).

  • hzdept_h: Top high value (may be missing).

  • hzdepb_r: Representative bottom depth.

  • hzdepb_l: Bottom low value (may be missing).

  • hzdepb_h: Bottom high value (may be missing).

Value

A data frame with missing depth variability values filled in. Missing top low values are replaced with hzdept_r - 2 and missing top high values with hzdept_r + 2. Similarly, missing bottom low values are replaced with hzdepb_r - 2 and missing bottom high values with hzdepb_r + 2. All values are ensured to be non-negative.

Examples

data <- data.frame(
  hzdept_r = c(10, 20),
  hzdept_l = c(NA, 18),
  hzdept_h = c(NA, NA),
  hzdepb_r = c(30, 40),
  hzdepb_l = c(NA, NA),
  hzdepb_h = c(NA, 42)
)
infill_missing_depth_variability(data)
#>   hzdept_r hzdept_l hzdept_h hzdepb_r hzdepb_l hzdepb_h
#> 1       10        8       12       30       28       32
#> 2       20       18       22       40       38       42
